**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The MINCOMMIT rule is satisfied at the **preferred** position — there is no take-or-pay, minimum volume, or shortfall penalty binding our side:

- **Discretionary funding:** Acquisition Account deposits are made by the Class A Certificateholder "solely at its option" (§4.4(d)(i), p0223); the Negative Carry deposit obligation is triggered only by that voluntary deposit (p0217).
- **Condition-based, not committed, acquisitions:** Additional Receivables transfers are "[s]ubject to the satisfaction of the conditions in Section 2.1(d)" — Transfer Notice, Credit Enhancement Test, Pool Composition Tests and Depositor certifications (p0037–p0043). Nothing obliges the Issuer to acquire receivables regardless of eligibility.
- **Pay-for-what-you-acquire:** the Issuer pays only the Additional Receivables Cash Transfer Amount for receivables actually acquired (p0224), and excess Acquisition Account / Negative Carry amounts are released to Certificateholders (p0225, p0220).
- **Clear exit:** on the first Payment Date of the Amortization Period all Acquisition Account and Negative Carry funds are swept to the Collection Account (p0226, p0221), ending the revolving purchase mechanic.
- **Direction check:** the only "shortfall" obligation in the document (p0211) runs *against* the Marketing Agent in our favour, and so is not flagged.

The Required Acquisition Deposit Amount and Required Negative Carry Amount are structural securitisation funding mechanics sized to voluntarily deposited cash — not commitments to purchase — so they fall outside this rule per the planner's note.
